q-120769.name: Question 1
q-120769.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14169002/assets/752bdd55a25b4949fc12ef1ddc68d57f3018617bbbbfd25812c664db606ae53f.png)

The perimeter $p$ of the equilateral triangle $△ABC$ is $18$ and the perimeter ${p}_{1}$ of the isosceles triangle $△ACD$ is $14.$ What is the measure of $\overset{―}{AD}?$
q-120769.worked_solution:
We're told that the perimeter of $△ABC$ is $p=18,$ and since all $3$ sides have equal length,  we get

$$
AC=\frac{p}{3}=\frac{18}{3}=6.
$$

For the perimeter ${p}_{1}$ of the isosceles triangle $△ACD,$ we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}_{1} & =AC+CD+AD \\ 14 & =AC+2AD \\ 14 & =6+2AD \\ 8 & =2AD \\ AD & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

q-20568.name: Question 2
q-20568.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14169002/assets/4ab3c4ba281be5363c5ea3e2b3fce6aec91221b31a762ef645c7262095866d5e.png)

The perimeter ${p}_{1}$ of the triangle $△DBC$ shown above is $10.$ What is the perimeter of the triangle $△ABC$ if $BD=3?$
q-20568.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we can see that $△ABC$ is an equilateral triangle and $△DBC$ is an isosceles triangle with $CD=DB.$

We're told that the perimeter of $△DBC$ is ${p}_{1}=10,$ and $DB=3,$ so we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{p}_{1} & =DB+BC+CD \\ 10 & =3+BC+3 \\ 4 & =BC.\end{aligned}
$$

So now we have enough information to compute the perimeter of the triangle $△ABC:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =3BC \\  & =3\cdot 4 \\  & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the perimeter of $△ABC$ is $p=12.$

q-67867.name: Question 3
q-67867.problem: In the regular heptagon $ABCDEFG$, we have $CD=2\,cm.$ What is the perimeter of the heptagon?
q-67867.worked_solution:
The perimeter $p$ of a polygon is the sum of the measures of all its sides. Since all the sides of a regular heptagon are equal and the measure of one of them is $2\,cm$, we have 

$$
p=7\cdot CD=7\cdot 2=14\,cm.
$$

q-357601.name: Question 5
q-357601.problem: An equilateral triangle has the same perimeter as a regular hexagon whose side is $5\,mm.$ Find the length of the side of the triangle.
q-357601.worked_solution:
Since all the sides of the hexagon are equal, its perimeter is

$$
p=6\cdot 5=30\,mm.
$$

Let $a$ be the side of the equilateral triangle. We know that our polygons have equal perimeters. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =3a \\ 30 & =3a \\ 10 & =a.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the side is $10\,mm.$

q-22633.problem: An equilateral triangle has the same perimeter as a regular decagon whose side is $6\,mm.$ Find the length of the side of the triangle.
q-22633.worked_solution:
Since all the sides of the decagon are equal, its perimeter is

$$
p=10\cdot 6=60\,mm.
$$

Let $a$ be the side of the equilateral triangle. We know that our polygons have equal perimeters. Therefore

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =3a \\ 60 & =3a \\ 20 & =a.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the length of the side is $20\,mm.$
